source.title: Skewness risk and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: The negative crypto asymmetry-risk premium is primarily idiosyncratic: assets with lower lagged market-residual skewness earn higher subsequent weekly returns.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact daily history and a valid residual-skewness estimate.
feature: For each asset and each Monday, estimate trailing-window beta to the contemporaneous equal-weight crypto market return using only prior completed UTC days. Compute residual returns r_i-beta*r_mkt and signal as negative skewness of those residuals.
signal_direction: Higher signal means lower idiosyncratic skewness; long highest-signal quintile and short lowest-signal quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: All feature and liquidity inputs end Sunday; rebalance Monday 00:00 UTC open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-signal-minus-low-signal spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 windows positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive total return at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 each non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper documents idiosyncratic asymmetry risk. This implementation uses a causal single-market-factor residual rather than a richer latent-factor model to keep the hypothesis simple, point-in-time, and reproducible.
